forbiddenPathViolationsJson / networkCallsObservedJson / fileSystemWritesObservedJson are documented and redacted as AGGREGATE descriptor arrays (e.g. {path, count} / {host, count}), never raw file contents or raw network payloads — consistent with 'network calls observed' / 'file-system writes observed' being observational summaries, not captured raw traffic.

SUPERSEDED by the 2026-08-21 repair (see `repair` block above): secret redaction no longer reuses `redactSecrets` from run_outcome_service.ts. That redactor only matches known TOKEN SHAPES and was never applied to the plain scalar columns (toolName/toolVersion/packageSource/installMethod/reason) at all — a repository write boundary that claims 'no secrets in any field' has to sanitize every field, not only the JSON blobs. Replaced with a dedicated `d1_secret_sanitizer.ts` applied to every column, including recursive secret-KEY detection inside JSON blobs (a shape `redactSecrets` never covered).

proposal_id carries a real FK to agent_org_proposals(id) (every ToolSafetyReport is only ever created for a real, already-persisted tool-install proposal by construction) but is deliberately NOT UNIQUE: a proposal may legitimately be re-vetted (e.g. after a sandbox_unavailable result), so findByProposalIdAsync returns the MOST RECENT report rather than enforcing one-report-per-proposal. SQLite orders by its real, monotonic implicit rowid (test-covered); Postgres orders by created_at DESC alone (ponytail: no cheap monotonic tiebreak exists on this table's random-UUID id column, and two reports for the same proposal committing within the same millisecond is not a realistic race for a human-triggered re-vet).
No new HTTP surface in this phase — D1.1 is model + repository + migration only, matching D2.1's precedent exactly. Wiring (sandbox vetter invocation, proposal lifecycle) is D1.2/D1.4.
